Here are the descriptions of the provided plots, following your guidelines:

The plot illustrates the relationship between iteration number and loss for different language model configurations. The x-axis is labeled “#Iteration” and has a linear scale ranging from 0 to 140000, with tick labels at intervals of 20000. The y-axis is labeled “Loss” and has a linear scale ranging from 2.4 to 3.4, with tick labels at intervals of 0.1. 

The first line, colored blue and labeled “Vanilla”, begins at approximately 3.3 at an iteration of 0 and decreases to approximately 2.52 at an iteration of 140000, exhibiting a steep decline in the first 20000 iterations and then leveling off. The second line, colored orange and labeled “StrmLLM (n=64)”, starts at approximately 3.28 at an iteration of 0 and decreases to approximately 2.53 at an iteration of 140000, with a similar decreasing trend to the first line. The third line, colored brown and labeled “SepLLM (n=64)”, begins at approximately 3.25 at an iteration of 0 and decreases to approximately 2.51 at an iteration of 140000, showing a similar decreasing trend. The fourth line, colored green and labeled “SepLLM (n=64, H)”, starts at approximately 3.23 at an iteration of 0 and decreases to approximately 2.50 at an iteration of 140000, with a similar decreasing trend. The fifth line, colored magenta and labeled “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)”, begins at approximately 3.22 at an iteration of 0 and decreases to approximately 2.49 at an iteration of 140000, exhibiting a similar decreasing trend. Finally, the sixth line, colored navy and labeled “SepLLM (n=128)”, starts at approximately 3.26 at an iteration of 0 and decreases to approximately 2.51 at an iteration of 140000, with a similar decreasing trend.
